newsitem.title: UK: ED & F Man sees strong Asian cocoa grind growth.
newsitem.headline: ED & F Man sees strong Asian cocoa grind growth.

text.p: Cocoa grindings in Asia are expected to grow by a strong eight percent in 1995/96 (Oct-Sept), outpacing an anticipated world growth of six percent, UK commodity house ED & F Man said in a report.
The six percent expansion in world grindings -- a measure of consumption -- would be the highest annual growth rate since 1988/89, it said in its September cocoa market report.
"In Asia, Japan is experiencing a boom in consumption of chocolate products following favourable press reports earlier in the year," Man said.
Japanese cocoa imports soared by 33.6 percent to 68,000 tonnes in beans equivalent from October 1995 to July 1996 from 50,900 in the same period a year ago, Man said.

"Overall, grindings in Asia are expected to grow by over eight percent this crop year despite a small decline in Malaysia, the region's largest bean processor, due to a shortage of locally-grown beans," it said.
Man last Thursday put 1995/96 world grindings at 2.69 million tonnes, up from 2.54 million in 1994/95.

It said second quarter 1996 grindings in the five largest processing countries -- the U.S., Brazil, the Netherlands, Germany and the UK -- exceeded its expectations by rising over 12 percent year-on-year.
